items.headline: Moody's France decision due after the US close (~3pm CT): Aa3 negative outlook, downgrade widely expected and priced in — the outlook (stable vs negative) is the FX variable (Reuters, Oct 23)
France 10Y 5.14% (highest since July 2002); OAT-Bund 170-177bp (highest since 2011) — French debt risk premium at euro-zone sovereign-crisis levels (Reuters/DJ Newswires, Oct 23)

WSJ/Reuters: US to remove 50% tariffs on some Canadian ag/forestry goods as early as Friday — proclamation unconfirmed, White House calls it speculation; Collins says 9 categories exempted; USD/CAD probing below 1.40 (Oct 23)
Gold broke below $4,000 to $3,986.50 (3-month low) before recovering to ~$4,005 — -3.5% weekly on oil-driven rate fears (Kitco/Reuters, Oct 23)
Brent ~$114.7-116 (5-6mo high), WTI ~$100 — Houthi missiles at Saudi interests; US-Iran rhetoric keeps the risk premium wide (zerohedge US open, Oct 23)
TD Securities dissents on BoC: hold at 2.25% in October, +25bp Dec and +25bp Jan — vs ~75-80% market pricing for an Oct-28 hike (FXStreet, Oct 23)
US 10Y 4.994% (+3.5bp) — steadied after Thursday's 19.5bp plunge; DXY ~101.7 off the 101.45 three-week low (baystreet/FXStreet, Oct 23)
U Mich final: sentiment 48.0 beat (vs 46.3 prelim — 2nd-lowest ever); 1-yr infl 4.7%, 5-yr 3.5% — highest since May (Reuters/WSJ, Oct 23)
US flash PMI: comp 57.6 inline (new orders 58.2 best since Mar-2022; output prices 59.8 hottest since Aug-2022) (Reuters, Oct 23)
Sterling at a fresh 17-month high vs the euro (EUR/GBP 0.8362, 4th straight weekly rise) after the UK flash PMI beat — BofA favors euro/pound, euro/yen, euro/CAD shorts
UK flash PMIs beat: comp 53.1 (vs 51.8 fcst, strongest since Feb) vs Sep retail sales -0.4% m/m miss (vs -0.1% fcst; Aug rev. up to +0.7%)
Eurozone growth slows to a 4-month low: Oct flash comp 51.9 (vs 52.7 fcst) — France back in contraction (48.9) amid political turmoil, rising energy-driven input costs
Euro depressed near 1.1200 vs a firming dollar — sellers out a second straight day after the weak flash PMIs
NZD/USD near 0.5700 on the RBNZ repricing — Oct-28 hike ~85% (Bloomberg via FXStreet; investinglive 99%)

Trump: Iran 'making up fake hits, mines, and everything else' to drive oil up ahead of the midterms; US moving a third carrier strike group toward the region; Saudi coalition intercepted 4 drones over Riyadh/Medina Thursday

Yen shines as AI jitters spur safe-haven rush: USD/JPY ~156.28 (yen's strongest in 1+ months), DXY 101.52, 10Y 4.953% — Nasdaq -2.6% (worst since June) on AI-capex doubts (Meta -7%, AMD -8%, Nvidia -4%); no dollar haven bid
Japan Sep core CPI 2.1% y/y inline — first print above BoJ's 2% target in nine months; core-core 2.4% (from 1.9%), services 1.5% (from 1.2%) — cements the near-term (December ~80%) hike case
UK GfK consumer confidence collapsed to -24 (vs -14 fcst) — biggest monthly drop since Apr 2020; inflation expectations at the highest since April

Aramco told staff to evacuate Dhahran HQ (first since the Iran war began) as Houthi strikes on Saudi energy infrastructure intensified — Brent settled $113.17 (+4.0%, highest since May 4), pushed above $114 in Asia

French debt risk premium reaches euro-zone sovereign crisis levels: OAT-Bund 173.58bp (widest since Nov 2011); 10Y OAT tested 5.14%; Macron banned Saturday's Lyon protests, deployed troops; Moody's reviews France Friday (Aa3 neg → A1 expected)
EZ consumer confidence -17.9 in October (vs -17.0 fcst; Sept rev. to -16.8) — second straight monthly fall as high energy costs keep households pessimistic
AU flash PMIs a big miss: composite 47.7, services 47.8, manufacturing 49.7 (first private-sector contraction in 5 months); input-cost inflation fastest since May
Japan flash PMIs: manufacturing 53.3 (7-month low, miss vs 54.5 fcst), services 52.0 up from 51.3, composite 52.3 (19th month of expansion)
RBA Nov-3 hike ~44-50% (LSEG ~42% Oct 21; Hauser: ~50% Oct 20 — 'inflation outlook worse'); December ~64%; Q3 CPI Oct 28 the pivot
US jobless claims 194K (vs 200K fcst; -6K; near 57-year lows); continuing claims 1.728M (+25K). Fed funds futures cut Oct-28 hike odds to ~11% (from ~13%)
Canada IPPI +2.0% m/m beat (vs 0.7% fcst; +14.5% y/y, 24th straight annual gain); RMPI +4.8% beat (vs 0.1%; +27.0% y/y) — upstream heat 6 days before the Oct-28 BoC
NZ Q3 CPI 0.7% q/q, 3.7% y/y — soft miss vs 0.8%/3.8% fcst (below RBNZ 3.9% proj; sector-factor core 2.8%) — hike stayed ~98% priced
